vorn.browser.name: read_page
vorn.browser.description: Read your session browser pane as an accessibility tree. Interactive elements carry a "ref" you can pass to browser_interact. Prefer this over screenshot: it is far cheaper and gives you actionable handles. Long pages paginate — pass the returned nextCursor back as `cursor`. When the page is a design artifact it also returns "artifact" (what the file declares) and "artifactValues" (what it is currently showing). Work from artifactValues: a person can turn a control without spending a turn, so the value on screen is routinely not the default in the file.

filter.description: "interactive" (default) returns only actionable elements; "all" adds text

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous read_page result

vorn.browser.name: get_page_text
vorn.browser.description: Read the visible text of your session browser pane. Use when you want to read an article or verify copy, rather than act on controls. Long pages paginate — pass the returned nextCursor back as `cursor`.

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous get_page_text result

vorn.browser.name: read_console_messages
vorn.browser.description: Read console output captured from your session browser pane since it opened.

vorn.browser.name: read_network_requests
vorn.browser.description: Read network requests captured from your session browser pane since it opened.

vorn.browser.name: browser_screenshot
vorn.browser.description: Capture your session browser pane as a PNG. This is the expensive last resort — reach for read_page first, and use this only when layout or rendering is the actual question.

vorn.browser.name: browser_find
vorn.browser.description: Find elements in your session browser pane whose accessible name contains some text. Cheaper than reading the whole page when you already know what you are looking for.

text.description: Text to match against element names (case-insensitive)

vorn.browser.name: browser_interact
vorn.browser.description: Act on your session browser pane: click, hover, type, press a key, or scroll. Address the target by "ref" from read_page where possible — refs survive reflow, coordinates do not. A ref from before a navigation is refused rather than guessed at; re-read the page. A ref target is scrolled into view first, so it does not need to be on screen already. "ok" means the input was dispatched, not that the page did what you expected — read the state back after anything that matters.

action.description: What to do. "type" clicks the target first when one is given.

x.description: Viewport x, when no ref is available

y.description: Viewport y, when no ref is available

text.description: Text for "type", or the key name for "key" (e.g. "Enter")

vorn.browser.name: open_browser_pane
vorn.browser.description: Open the browser pane for your session, optionally at a URL. You do not need a person to open it for you. Opening a pane that already exists just points it at the URL.

url.description: URL to open (defaults to the pane's start page)

vorn.browser.name: browser_tabs
vorn.browser.description: List, add, close, or switch tabs in your session browser pane. "close" and "select" take a zero-based index — call "list" first to see what those indices name, since a tab that redirected or followed a link is no longer on the page it was opened with. Closing the last remaining tab closes the pane.

vorn.browser.name: browser_navigate
vorn.browser.description: Navigate your session browser pane to a URL. Opens the pane first if none is open. http and https, plus file: urls inside your session's own project or worktree — anything outside it is refused, so serve files from elsewhere over http instead. The pane carries no claude.ai login, so artifact URLs will not load in it.

vorn.browser.name: browser_history
vorn.browser.description: Step back or forward through your session browser pane's own history — the same thing the pane's back and forward buttons do. Fails when there is no page to move to, rather than quietly staying put.

vorn.device.name: device_list
vorn.device.description: List the iOS simulators on this machine, with their state and which session (if any) has claimed each. The only device tool that works before you claim anything — start here.

vorn.device.name: device_claim
vorn.device.description: Claim a simulator for your session, booting it if needed. Every other device tool acts on your claimed device. Claiming one another session holds fails and names the holder — two agents driving one screen produce results that look like app bugs.

vorn.device.name: device_release
vorn.device.description: Release your claimed simulator so another session can use it. A simulator Vorn booted is shut down; one that was already running when you claimed it is left alone.

vorn.device.name: read_screen
vorn.device.description: Read your claimed simulator as an accessibility tree. Elements carry a "ref" you can pass to device_interact. Prefer this over device_screenshot: it is far cheaper and gives you handles rather than pixels. Coordinates are in POINTS, which is what taps take — a screenshot is typically 3x larger in pixels. Long screens paginate via nextCursor.

filter.description: "interactive" (default) returns only actionable elements; "all" adds text

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous read_screen result

vorn.device.name: device_find
vorn.device.description: Find elements on your claimed simulator whose label or accessibility identifier contains some text. Searches the whole screen, not just the first page read_screen would return.

text.description: Text to match against labels and identifiers (case-insensitive)

vorn.device.name: device_interact
vorn.device.description: Act on your claimed simulator: tap, swipe, type, press a hardware button, long-press, or rotate it. Address the target by "ref" from read_screen where possible. Coordinates are in POINTS. A ref from before an earlier interaction is refused rather than guessed at — read the screen again. A swipe starting at the very edge of the screen is refused too: iOS claims those as system gestures and swallows them, which looks to you like nothing happened.

action.description: "press" is a long press; "button" takes a name in `text`; "rotate" takes `orientation`

ref.description: Element ref from read_screen or device_find

x.description: Screen x in points, when no ref is available

y.description: Screen y in points, when no ref is available

text.description: Text for "type", or the button name for "button" (HOME, LOCK, SIRI, SIDE_BUTTON)

orientation.description: Which way up to turn the device, for "rotate"

system_gesture.description: Allow a stroke starting in the bezel band, when a system gesture is the intent

vorn.device.name: device_screenshot
vorn.device.description: Capture your claimed simulator as a downscaled PNG. The expensive last resort — reach for read_screen first, and use this only when layout or rendering is the actual question. The result reports the scale factor: divide an image coordinate by it to get the point coordinate device_interact takes.

max_edge.description: Longest edge of the returned image in pixels (default 1000)

vorn.device.name: device_launch
vorn.device.description: Launch an installed app on your claimed simulator by bundle id.

vorn.device.name: device_terminate
vorn.device.description: Terminate a running app on your claimed simulator by bundle id.

vorn.device.name: device_install
vorn.device.description: Install a built .app bundle on your claimed simulator. Takes a path to an already-built bundle; it does not build anything for you.

vorn.device.name: device_open_url
vorn.device.description: Open a URL on your claimed simulator — a web URL in Safari, or a custom scheme to exercise deep links into an app.

url.description: URL or custom-scheme link to open

vorn.device.name: device_logs
vorn.device.description: Read log output captured from your claimed simulator since it was claimed.

vorn.device.name: open_device_pane
vorn.device.description: Open the device pane for your session so the person can watch. You do not need this to drive a simulator — every other device tool works with the pane closed.

udid.description: Simulator to show (defaults to your claimed one)
